messages:
maria: FYI a customer flagged an unexpected billing delta after a streaming request retried during a router failover. Appears like two provisional entries were billed instead of one final. File logs attached.

ahmed: paste logs + model/route?

maria: model=rwd-3b-quant, route=us-east-1-preemptible. Snippet: `2026-04-02T09:12:01Z start session=sess-7 seq=0`, `2026-04-02T09:12:02Z router hop id=null -> new`, `2026-04-02T09:12:02Z toolcall ack=58 client_eof=true truncated=true`, `2026-04-02T09:12:03Z provisional_ledger row_id=pv-900 tokens=210`, `2026-04-02T09:12:04Z final_ledger row_id=fn-901 tokens=72 confirmed=true`

jules: so final is smaller than provisional but customer shows both. Did tombstone get emitted to mark pv-900 stale?

maria: console shows pv-900 + fn-901. Net billed = 210 in the invoice, so final didn't replace provisional.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-1510 opened and assigned to @jules.

jules: root cause hypothesis: we optimistically emit provisional when a new route claims the session. If that claim is followed by a truncate event, the runtime should emit a tombstone pointing to the provisional row. Looks like tombstone wasn't emitted or lost.

kai: runtime note: current routing protocol generates an ephemeral `route_claim_id` but it's only in memory. On reconnect the client router reissues a new claim id. Without a durable handoff id we can't correlate across claims.

ahmed: proposal: introduce durable header `X-Handoff-ID` that survives reconnects and stays on the client side for the life of the request. Ledger rows (provisional/final/tombstone) get this handoff id. Then de-duping is straightforward.

sam: console implications: we need to fold rows by handoff_id at invoice rendering time. Also show a timeline for the request: [provisional -> tombstone? -> final]. Add a small icon explaining tombstone semantics.

jules: implementation detail: tombstone event should contain `prev_row_id` and `prev_tokens` so accounting can assert the tombstone cancels the exact provisional. We also need to ensure tombstone is emitted before any confirm so UI doesn't flicker. Ordering matters.

kai: can the runtime emit tombstone synchronously? There are races during handoff where both old and new shard attempt confirm. We should use a compare-and-swap on ledger write using handoff_id to guarantee single winner.

ahmed: telemetry ask: add `ledger.tombstone.created` counter and `ledger.tombstone.apply_latency_ms` histogram. Dashboards: tombstone_rate by route, tombstone_vs_provisional_ratio, and a panel listing sessions with multiple active entries. Alert if tombstone_ratio < 80% when provisional>final in a route (indicates missing tombstones).

maria: product: customers will panic if they suddenly see more lines. Default console behavior: collapse provisional+final into single line if they share handoff_id, but show an option to expand. Also add a billing note to clarify provisional rows are optimistic and final is authoritative.

sam: rollout plan: 1) runtime: propagate X-Handoff-ID and emit tombstone events on truncation (canary servicers). 2) ledger: accept tombstone entries and make them queryable via handoff_id. 3) console: fold by handoff_id and surface a toggle. 4) refunds: manual reconciliation only initially.

jules: testing: fuzz handoff scenarios with interleaved confirms and tombstones. Add unit tests for ledger CAS behavior and integration test that simulates network flaps.

kai: edgecases: prefetch/background embeddings may create separate sessions without preserving handoff_id. We must pass handoff_id to child requests or attach parent_handoff_id so invoices can group.

ahmed: we also need to audit historical rows. Script to backfill handoff_id for sessions with single route may be possible, but multi-route cases will remain unresolved. Add backfill GH task.

maria: product OK with approach. Schedule a quick sync Wed 11:30 to map telemetry dashboards and decide alert thresholds. Owners: runtime=kai, ledger=jules, console=sam, product=maria.

jules: quick question about header name. `X-Handoff-ID` is fine but prefer lower-case header `x-handoff-id` in code. Also expose `x-handoff-reason` as optional human-friendly string.

kai: ack runtime owner. I'll add the header to the router and update client lib to persist it across reconnects.

sam: ack console. I'll prototype folding logic and default collapse.

ahmed: ack infra. Created GH issue rwd/infra#4602 with acceptance criteria and test matrix.

maria: thanks everyone. Logging task + dashboards are priority for the canary. I'll update INC-2026-1510 with links and next steps.
